subject: Combining bifactor model with second order factor model

messages.author: 6855b04443295af7
messages.subject: Combining bifactor model with second order factor model
parts:
Hello! 

We are evaluating a clinical survey where it seems feasible to combine the bifactor model with the second-order factor model. But I wonder if this is something that is sensible? 

For example, 
  • 1 overall psychological trait explained by 3 sub-traits 
  • 3 specific factors

So it will look something like this in the model. 

hybrid = "
            # 3 traits
             A =~ x1 + x2 + x3
             B =~ x4 + x5 + x6
             C =~ x7 + x8 + x9

           # overall trait
              GEN =~ A + B + C

          # specific factors
             S1 =~ x1 + x4 + x7
             S2 =~ x2 + x5 + x8
             S3 =~ x3 + x6 + x9

          #orthogonal
             S1 ~~ 0*S2
             S1 ~~ 0*S3
             S2 ~~ 0*S3
             S1 ~~ 0*A
             S2 ~~ 0*A
             S3 ~~ 0*A
             S1 ~~ 0*B
             S2 ~~ 0*B
             S3 ~~ 0*B
             S1 ~~ 0*C
             S2 ~~ 0*C
             S3 ~~ 0*C

"

hybrid_mod <- cfa(model = hybrid, data = dis_items, estimator='mlr', verbose = TRUE)

We tested the model and it converges with good parameter estimates, but have yet to see any paper published using such an approach. But we might not be looking hard enough. It would be great if someone to point us to some literature on this. 
We considered using just a GEN factor instead of a second-order approach in the bifactor model, but the model fit was very poor, and they were theoretically distinct but related constructs. 
We do acknowledge that the loadings for GEN on A,B,C is very high, ranging from .8 to .9, and we weren't sure if this is a correct approach. 
We would appreciate some guidance on this. 

Kind regards,
Aiden

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Combining bifactor model with second order factor model
parts:
I would call this a multitrait-multimethod (MTMM) model rather than a bifactor model, although MTMM is essentially a bifactor model with more than 1 trait factor.  Perhaps the MTMM keyword will turn up more research.  You could also ask on the more general SEM forum SEMNET:

https://listserv.ua.edu/cgi-bin/wa?SUBED1=semnet&A=1
